qc_e_les_surplombs.blurb: Les surplombs is a steep, bolted sector on the gneiss cliff of Pic aux Corbeaux in Orford park, in Quebec's Eastern Townships. All twenty lines are sport climbs and the level is high: a few at 5.11, a handful at 5.12, and the bulk at 5.13 with several in the 5.14 range. Many lines begin on a nearly vertical slab before reaching a leaning wall, so expect sharp crimps and sustained pulling rather than easy warm-ups. The rock is solid but can feel rough on the skin, and it may be damp in places. This is a spot for strong climbers working projects, with space left for new development.

qc_6_main_wall.blurb: The Main Wall is the sector at Mont Rigaud, a granite cliff in the Montérégie, that holds the tallest lines on the hill. Nineteen of its twenty routes are bolted sport climbs, with a single trad line, and they run from very easy up to 5.11. Roughly a quarter sit around 5.8, and another cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, so there is something for newer leaders and for those pushing harder. Neighbouring walls offer easy top-rope setups, which makes the area a good day out with mixed-ability partners. Weekends bring crowds on the moderates, while weekdays are quiet.

qc_b_cronos.blurb: Cronos is the second wall along the trail at Chez Roger, a gneiss cliff in the Lanaudière region north of Montréal. Twelve of its twenty routes are trad and eight are sport, covering 5.7 through 5.13. Most of the lines fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with a handful of mid-grade trad climbs that suit climbers stepping up and a few hard sport pitches at the top end. The walk from the parking lot is brief, so it works well as a first or second stop for a day. The rock is thin, rough bands, so bring tape for your fingers.

qc_louise_boulder.blurb: Louise Boulder is a single, well-loved block in the Val-David boulder fields of the Laurentians, within the regional park. It carries twenty problems across the full range, from a few easy slabby lines near V1, through a solid middle of V4 to V7, up to a couple of V9 and a V11 test piece. Among Val-David boulders it is regarded as second only to Élizabeth for quality lines, so it draws steady traffic. The Laurentian granite favours technical movement, and the approach from the lot is short, making it easy to combine with neighbouring blocks.

ri_pond_cave.blurb: Pond Cave is a long, steep band of granite on the edge of the pond in Lincoln Woods State Park, north of Providence. It is one of the more powerful spots in the park, with 26 boulder problems that start near V1 and run up to V11. Most climbers will find their level in the V3 to V4 range or among the harder V8 and V9 lines. Expect a good deal of roof and traverse climbing. Sun reaches the cave in winter and it is cooler in summer, though bugs can be fierce in warm months, and the low landing can flood at times.
